readings.title: Abner Defects to Dawid
readings.subtitle: A Covenant at Hebron
readings.text: [2 Samuel 3:6] And it came to be, while there was war between the house of Sha’ul and the house of Dawid, that Aḇnĕr was strengthening his hold on the house of Sha’ul. [7] And Sha’ul had a concubine, whose name was Ritspah, the daughter of Ayah. And Ishbosheth said to Aḇnĕr, “Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?” [8] And Aḇnĕr was very wroth at the words of Ishbosheth, and said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Yehudah? Today I show loving-commitment to the house of Sha’ul your father, to his brothers, and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the hand of Dawid, and you charge me today with a fault concerning this woman? [9] “Let <dn>Elohim</dn> do so to Aḇnĕr, and more also, if I do not do for him as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has sworn to Dawid, [10] to transfer the reign from the house of Sha’ul, and set up <dn>את</dn> the throne of Dawid over Yisra’ĕl and over Yehudah, from Dan to Be’ĕr Sheḇa.” [11] And he was unable to answer <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr another word, because he feared him. [12] And Aḇnĕr sent messengers on his behalf to Dawid, saying, “Whose is the land?” saying also, “Make your covenant with <dn>את</dn> me, and see, my hand is with you to bring <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl to you.” [13] And he said, “Good, I make a covenant with <dn>את</dn> you. But one matter I ask of you, namely: you do not see my face unless you first bring <dn>את</dn> Miḵal, Sha’ul’s daughter, when you come to see <dn>את</dn> my face.” [14] And Dawid sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Sha’ul’s son, saying, “Give me <dn>את</dn> my wife Miḵal, to whom I became engaged for a hundred foreskins of the Pelishtites.” [15] And Ishbosheth sent and took her from her husband, from Palti’ĕl son of Layish. [16] And her husband went with her, weeping as he went behind her to Baḥurim. And Aḇnĕr said to him, “Go, return!” And he returned. [17] And Aḇnĕr had a word with the elders of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “In times past you were seeking for <dn>את</dn> Dawid to be sovereign over you. [18] “And now, do it! For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken of Dawid, saying, ‘<dq>By the hand of <dn>My</dn> servant Dawid, <dn>I</dn> save <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ĕl from the hand of the Pelishtites and from the hand of all their enemies.</dq>’ ” [19] And Aḇnĕr also spoke in the hearing of Binyamin. And Aḇnĕr also went to speak in the hearing of Dawid in Ḥeḇron <dn>את</dn> all that seemed good to Yisra’ĕl and all the whole house of Binyamin. [20] And Aḇnĕr came to Dawid at Ḥeḇron, and with him twenty men. And Dawid made a feast for Aḇnĕr and the men who were with <dn>את</dn> him. [21] And Aḇnĕr said to Dawid, “Let me arise and go, and gather <dn>את</dn> all Yisra’ĕl to my master the sovereign, so that they make a covenant with <dn>את</dn> you, and you shall reign over all that your heart desires.” And Dawid sent <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr away, and he went in peace.

readings.title: The Murder of Abner
readings.subtitle: Yoab's Revenge
readings.text: [2 Samuel 3:22] And see, the servants of Dawid and Yo’aḇ came from a raid, and brought much spoil with them. But Aḇnĕr was not with Dawid in Ḥeḇron, for he had sent him away, and he had gone in peace. [23] When Yo’aḇ and all the army that was with him came, they told Yo’aḇ, saying, “Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr came to the sovereign, and he sent him away, and he went in peace.” [24] And Yo’aḇ came to the sovereign and said, “What have you done? See, Aḇnĕr came to you! Why did you send him away, so that he is already gone? [25] “You know <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr, that he came to deceive you, and to know <dn>את</dn> your going out and <dn>את</dn> your coming in, and to know <dn>את</dn> all that you are doing.” [26] And Yo’aḇ came out from Dawid, and he sent messengers after Aḇnĕr, who brought <dn>את</dn> him back from the well of Sirah. But Dawid did not know it. [27] And when Aḇnĕr had returned to Ḥeḇron, Yo’aḇ took him aside in the gate to speak with <dn>את</dn> him privately, and there smote him in the stomach, so that he died for the blood of Asahĕl his brother. [28] And afterwards, when Dawid heard it, he said, “My reign and I are guiltless before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forever of the blood of Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr. [29] “Let it rest on the head of Yo’aḇ and on all his father’s house. And let there never fail to be in the house of Yo’aḇ one who has a discharge or is a leper, who leans on a staff or falls by the sword, or who lacks bread.” [30] So Yo’aḇ and Aḇishai his brother killed Aḇnĕr, because he had put to death <dn>את</dn> their brother Asahĕl at Giḇ‛on in the battle.

readings.title: Dawid Mourns for Abner
readings.subtitle: A Prince Falls in Yisra'el
readings.text: [2 Samuel 3:31] And Dawid said to Yo’aḇ and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your garments, and gird yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn for Aḇnĕr.” And Sovereign Dawid followed the bier. [32] And they buried <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron. And the sovereign lifted up <dn>את</dn> his voice and wept at the grave of Aḇnĕr, and all the people wept. [33] And the sovereign lamented over Aḇnĕr and said, “Should Aḇnĕr die as a fool dies? [34] “Your hands were not bound nor your feet put into bronze shackles. As one falls before sons of wickedness, so you fell.” And all the people wept over him again. [35] And all the people came to cause <dn>את</dn> Dawid to eat food while it was still day, but Dawid swore, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread or whatever else till the sun goes down!” [36] And all the people took note of it, and it was good in their eyes, since whatever the sovereign did was good in the eyes of all the people. [37] And all the people and all Yisra’ĕl knew that day that it had not been the sovereign’s purpose to put to death <dn>את</dn> Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr. [38] And the sovereign said to his servants, “Do you not know that a prince and a great man has fallen in Yisra’ĕl today? [39] “And I am weak today, though anointed sovereign. And these men, the sons of Tseruyah, are too harsh for me. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> repay the evildoer according to his evil.”

readings.title: Panic in the House of Sha'ul
readings.subtitle: The Captains of the Troops
readings.text: [2 Samuel 4:1] And when Sha’ul’s son heard that Aḇnĕr had died in Ḥeḇron, his hands became feeble, and all Yisra’ĕl was troubled. [2] And Sha’ul’s son had two men, captains of troops. The name of one was Ba‛anah and the name of the other Rĕḵaḇ, the sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, of the children of Binyamin – for Be’ĕroth is also reckoned to Binyamin, [3] because the Be’ĕrothites fled to Gittayim and have been sojourners there until this day.

readings.title: The Assassination of Ishbosheth
readings.subtitle: Dawid Executes Justice
readings.text: [2 Samuel 4:5] And the sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, Rĕḵaḇ and Ba‛anah, went and came at about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who was lying on his bed at noon. [6] And they came there, into the midst of the house, fetching wheat. And they smote him in the stomach, and Rĕḵaḇ and Ba‛anah his brother escaped. [7] For when they came into the house, he was lying on his bed in his bedroom. And they smote him, and killed him, and beheaded him, and took <dn>את</dn> his head, and went by the way of the Araḇah all night. [8] And they brought <dn>את</dn> the head of Ishbosheth to Dawid at Ḥeḇron, and said to the sovereign, “Here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of Sha’ul your enemy, who sought <dn>את</dn> your life. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has avenged my master the sovereign this day of Sha’ul and his seed.” [9] And Dawid answered Rĕḵaḇ and Ba‛anah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Be’ĕrothite, and said to them, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> lives, who has redeemed <dn>את</dn> my life from all distress, [10] when someone told me, saying, ‘See, Sha’ul is dead,’ thinking to have brought good news, I laid hold of him and killed him in Tsiqlag, which was the reward I gave him for his news. [11] “How much more, when wrong men have killed a righteous person in his own house on his bed? And now, should I not require <dn>את</dn> his blood at your hand and remove <dn>את</dn> you from the earth?” [12] And Dawid commanded his young men, and they killed them, and cut off <dn>את</dn> their hands and <dn>את</dn> feet, and hanged them by the pool in Ḥeḇron. And they took <dn>את</dn> the head of Ishbosheth and buried it in the burial-site of Aḇnĕr in Ḥeḇron.
